title: Security Groups
explanation: Security groups act as virtual firewalls for your instances, controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. They are stateful — if you allow inbound traffic, the response is automatically allowed outbound.
analogy: Security groups are like bouncers at a club — they check every person (packet) against the guest list (rules) before allowing entry or exit.
keyPoints: Security groups are stateful — return traffic is automatically allowed
Default: all inbound denied, all outbound allowed
You can only specify allow rules, not deny rules
Security groups are associated with ENIs (network interfaces)

examKeywords.definition: A stateful virtual firewall controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the instance (ENI) level. Supports allow rules only.

commonMistakes: Confusing security groups (stateful, instance-level) with NACLs (stateless, subnet-level)
Not understanding that security groups can reference other security groups as sources
